definitions.explanation: Protective body covering worn by warriors, especially the traditional Japanese armor worn by samurai. Also used figuratively for emotional defenses or outward facades.

examples.japanese: ⟦{博物館|はくぶつかん}→博物館：01494_hakubutsukan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{鎧|よろい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{展示|てんじ}→展示：12401_tenji⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Armor is on display at the museum.

examples.japanese: ⟦{武士|ぶし}→武士：03989_bushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鎧|よろい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧につけて⟦{戦|たたか}った→戦う：02071_tatakau⟧。

⟦{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}→端午の節句：16518_tangonosekku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鎧|よろい}や⟦{兜|かぶと}→兜：11625_kabuto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧⟦{家庭|かてい}→家庭：12315_katei⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Some families display armor and helmets for the Boys' Day festival.

notes:
Refers specifically to Japanese-style armor unless otherwise qualified. Western-style armor is usually distinguished as ⟦{西洋|せいよう}→西洋：01446_seiyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鎧|よろい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鎧|よろい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧ / {鎧|よろい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{身|み}につける→身につける：03158_minitsukeru⟧ (to put on armor)
- {鎧|よろい}{兜|かぶと} (armor and helmet — a set phrase)
- {鎧|よろい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}ぐ→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧ (to remove armor; figuratively, to drop one's guard)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese armor ({鎧|よろい}) is displayed during ⟦{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}→端午の節句：16518_tangonosekku⟧ (Boys' Day, May 5) as a symbol of strength and protection for boys.
